phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسٖ وَٰحِدَةٖ وَخَلَقَ مِنۡهَا زَوۡجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنۡهُمَا رِجَالٗا كَثِيرٗا وَنِسَآءٗۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡحَامَۚ
phrases.translation: O humanity! Be mindful of your Lord Who created you from a single soul, and from it He created its mate, and through both He spread countless men and women. And be mindful of Allah—in Whose Name you appeal to one
phrases.explanation:
"O humanity! Be mindful of your Lord Who created you from a single soul, and from it He created its mate, and through both He spread countless men and women. Be mindful of Allah through Whom you ask one another, and be mindful of the ties of kinship. Surely Allah is ever Watchful over you."

Allah addresses all mankind and reminds them of His favor: fear your Lord, who created you from one soul, namely Adam, and from that soul He created its mate, Eve, and from the two of them He spread forth many men and women across the earth. The exegetes said this teaches that all people are descended from one pair, so they are brothers and should treat one another with mercy, and that the guardian should fear Allah in the orphan's affairs. Some said "a single soul" means Adam alone, and the man is meant by the feminine form because of the word that follows, as happens in Arabic poetry.

"Be mindful of Allah through Whom you ask one another": when one of you asks another for something, he asks by the name of Allah as well, so fear Allah and do not swear by Him falsely. The reciters differed over the doubling or lightening of this word, and both are well-known recitations with no difference in meaning. "And the ties of kinship": fear Allah in your dealings with your relatives and do not sever the bonds of kinship, for severing them is a great sin. "Surely Allah is ever Watchful over you": He sees all your deeds and knows your intentions, and He will requite you for them, so fear Him in secret and in public, and do not let Satan call you to severing kinship or to sin. And He reminds you that He is the Creator of all, so worship Him alone and do not associate partners with Him.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ رَقِيبٗا
phrases.translation: another—and ˹honour˺ family ties. Surely Allah is ever Watchful over you
phrases.explanation: "Surely Allah is ever Watchful over you." He sees all that you do, in secret and in public, and nothing is hidden from Him. He knows the one who severs kinship and the one who keeps it, the one who asks by His name falsely and the one who is truthful, and He will requite each according to his deeds on the Day of Judgment. So fear Him, keep the ties of kinship, and ask one another only in truth, for the Watchful Lord sees you always. And do not let anyone call you to disobey Him. And He is the best of watchers. Do good and Allah will see it.

phrases.ar: وَءَاتُواْ ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰٓ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡۖ وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُواْ ٱلۡخَبِيثَ بِٱلطَّيِّبِۖ وَلَا تَأۡكُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَمۡوَٰلِكُمۡۚ
phrases.translation: Give orphans their wealth ˹when they reach maturity˺, and do not exchange your worthless possessions for their valuables, nor cheat them by mixing their wealth
phrases.explanation:
"Give orphans their wealth when they reach maturity, and do not exchange your worthless possessions for their valuables, nor cheat them by consuming their wealth."

Allah commands the guardians of orphans to hand over the orphans' wealth when they reach maturity and become able to manage it, and not to swap the bad of their own property for the good of the orphan's, nor to consume the orphan's wealth by mixing it with their own and eating from it. The exegetes differed over the manner of the cheating: some said the guardians would take the precious and valuable from the orphan's property and put in its place the worthless and inferior, and others said they would eat the orphan's food along with their own, and others that they would spend lavishly from it on themselves. Either way the ruling is the same: the orphan's wealth is a trust, and whoever consumes it unjustly sins greatly.

"Surely those who devour up the orphans' wealth unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies. Surely Allah has prepared for them a blazing Fire": that devouring is counted as eating fire, for it will burn them in the Hereafter, and Allah has prepared a blazing, flaming Fire for them on the Day of Judgment, and they will abide in it forever. So fear Allah, O guardians, and return the wealth to its owners.

phrases.ar: إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حُوبٗا كَبِيرٗا
phrases.translation: with your own. For this would indeed be a great sin
phrases.explanation: "Surely those who devour up the orphans' wealth unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies. Surely Allah has prepared for them a blazing Fire." Whoever eats the orphan's wealth unjustly only fills his belly with fire that will blaze in him on the Day of Judgment. The Fire is prepared for them and it is blazing, and they will abide in it, and no wealth they gathered will avail them then. This is a severe warning to every guardian, so return the trusts to their owners and fear the All-Seeing Lord. So be a trustworthy guardian and fear Allah. And He will not wrong you if you are honest.

phrases.ar: وَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا تُقۡسِطُواْ فِي ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ مَثۡنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَۖ فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْ فَوَٰحِدَةً أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۚ
phrases.translation: If you fear you might fail to give orphan women their ˹due˺ rights ˹if you were to marry them˺, then marry other women of your choice—two, three, or four. But if you are afraid you will fail to maintain justice, then ˹content yourselves with˺ one or
phrases.explanation:
"If you fear you might fail to give orphan women their due rights if you were to marry them, then marry other women who are good to you, two, three, or four. But if you fear you will not be just, then marry only one, or what your right hands possess. That is more likely to prevent you from committing an injustice."

Allah says to the guardians of orphan girls: if you fear that you cannot be just toward the female orphans under your care, whether in the dowry or in treatment, if you were to marry them, then marry from other women what is good and permissible to you, two, three, or four. The exegetes differed over the meaning of this fear: some said it is a prohibition of marrying more than four out of concern for the orphan's property, others that the people felt burdened over the orphan's wealth and so were told to marry other women, others that just as you fear for the orphans, fear likewise for the women lest you commit injustice with them, and others that the verse means: if you fear not being just toward the female orphans, then marry other women. The most appropriate view is that the verse permits marriage to other women so that the guardian does not wrong the orphan girl by marrying her while fearing injustice toward her.

"But if you fear you will not be just, then marry only one, or what your right hands possess": if you fear you cannot do justice among several wives, then limit yourself to one wife, or to a bondwoman, which is easier and involves less risk of injustice. "That is more likely to prevent you from committing an injustice": the restriction to one is nearer to justice, for justice among co-wives is difficult and rarely achieved. And Allah knows what is in your hearts and will hold you to account for it, so fear Him in this matter and be just. "The orphans" here covers both male and female orphans. "Marry the women who please you" means marry what is lawful to you of the women, two, three, or four, for Allah has permitted that, but justice among them is required. The grammar of the verse shows an implied answer: if you fear injustice toward the orphans, the response is to marry other women instead, so that you do not wrong the orphan ward. And the equity required is justice in spending and treatment, for Allah knows what is in the hearts and will judge between His servants on the Day of Judgment.

phrases.ar: ذَٰلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعُولُواْ
phrases.translation: those ˹bondwomen˺ in your possession. This way you are less likely to commit injustice
phrases.explanation: "That is more likely to prevent you from committing an injustice." The choice of a single wife, or of a bondwoman, is closer to justice than marrying many, for equality among co-wives in love, spending, and lodging is difficult, and the one who fears Allah will incline to what is safer. Whoever is just will be rewarded, and whoever wrongs will be called to account, for Allah is All-Knowing of what you do and All-Seeing of your hearts. And do not wrong the orphan women in their dowries or their persons. And He guides whom He wills to justice. So marry what is good and be just.

phrases.ar: وَءَاتُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ صَدُقَٰتِهِنَّ نِحۡلَةٗۚ فَإِن طِبۡنَ لَكُمۡ عَن شَيۡءٖ مِّنۡهُ
phrases.translation: Give women ˹you wed˺ their due dowries graciously. But if they waive some of it willingly, then you
phrases.explanation:
"Give women you wed their due dowries graciously."

Allah commands the husbands to give their wives the bridal dues, the mahr, as a free gift. "Nihla" means a bestowal given willingly and freely, a duty owed by the man to the woman at the time of marriage, and it belongs to the wife alone, not to her guardian. The exegetes differed over details: some said the verse was addressed to the guardians of women, because in the pre-Islamic era a man would give his ward to another man in exchange for a dowry, taking the mahr himself, and so Allah commanded that the mahr be given to the woman herself. Others said the verse is a command to the husbands of women with whom the union has been consummated, to give the dowry that was assigned.

"But if they waive some of it willingly, then you may enjoy it freely with a clear conscience": if the wife, of her own free will and without coercion, gives up some of her mahr to her husband, then he may take it, and it is lawful for him, and "hanni" and "mari" mean pleasant and wholesome in enjoyment. Some said this also refers to the guardians: if the women whose marriage is arranged waive some of the mahr to the guardian, he may take it. But the general ruling is that the mahr is the woman's right, and whatever she gives willingly is a gift. And Allah is All-Knowing of what you do, so give willingly and accept willingly, and do not wrong the women in their dowries.

phrases.ar: نَفۡسٗا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيٓـٔٗا مَّرِيٓـٔٗا
phrases.translation: may enjoy it freely with a clear conscience
phrases.explanation: "But if they waive some of it willingly, then you may enjoy it freely with a clear conscience." If the wife gives the husband some of her dowry of her own free choice, without compulsion, then he may enjoy it, and it is wholesome and lawful for him, for Allah has made it permissible. The condition is that her waiver be willing, with a sound mind, so that no injustice occurs. And Allah is All-Knowing of the intentions of both, and He will requite each for what he intended, so be generous in giving and honest in taking. And fear the Lord of the worlds in this matter.

phrases.ar: وَلَا تُؤۡتُواْ ٱلسُّفَهَآءَ أَمۡوَٰلَكُمُ ٱلَّتِي جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ قِيَٰمٗا وَٱرۡزُقُوهُمۡ فِيهَا وَٱكۡسُوهُمۡ
phrases.translation: Do not entrust the incapable ˹among your dependants˺ with your wealth which Allah has made a means of support for you—but feed and clothe them
phrases.explanation:
"Do not entrust the incapable among your dependants with your wealth which Allah has made a means of support for you, but feed them and clothe them from it and speak to them graciously."

Allah forbids the guardians to hand over to the foolish the wealth that Allah has made a means of support and standing for them. "The incapable" are those who cannot manage wealth and will waste it. The exegetes differed over who they are: some said they are the women and the children, others that they are exclusively the children, others the foolish among the children, and others that in this place they are exclusively the women. The correct view is that it is the one who deserves interdiction, the spendthrift who squanders his wealth and does not guard it, whether young or old, male or female, for the verse is general.

So the guardian should not give the wealth to the foolish one, but should spend on him from it, feed and clothe him, and speak to him graciously, for good speech is part of good treatment. "Which Allah has made a means of support for you": wealth is a trust and a means of standing in society, and squandering it brings poverty and disgrace. And "speak to them graciously": kind words soften the heart and are part of spending on them in a good manner. And test them until they show sound judgment, then hand over the wealth, as Allah commands in the verse of the orphans. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do, so manage the wealth well and fear Him in the affair of the incapable. "Your possessions, which Allah has made for you a means of standing": the exegetes differed over whether the foolish meant here are the women and the children together, or the children only, or the women only, but Allah issued a general prohibition against giving the foolish all possessions, so the meaning is the one who squanders and does not guard, whoever he is. And those whose guardians were commanded to hand over their possessions to them are those who show sound judgment, for the wealth is a trust and must be managed well, and Allah sees how you manage it. And whoever manages well will be rewarded, and whoever wastes will be blamed. Spend on them with moderation, neither extravagant nor miserly, and remember that every coin is a trust from Allah that you will be asked about on the Day of Judgment.

phrases.ar: وَقُولُواْ لَهُمۡ قَوۡلٗا مَّعۡرُوفٗا
phrases.translation: from it, and speak to them kindly
phrases.explanation: "But feed them and clothe them from it and speak to them graciously." The guardian spends on the incapable one from the wealth, providing food and clothing, and speaks to him with kind and gentle words, for harshness is not fitting where kindness suffices. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do, so treat your dependants with mercy and good conduct, spend on them from what He has given you, and fear Him in all your dealings with them. And do not expose them to poverty or harshness. And the best of speech is the kind word. And Allah loves those who treat their dependants kindly. And He is with you wherever you are.

phrases.ar: وَٱبۡتَلُواْ ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغُواْ ٱلنِّكَاحَ فَإِنۡ ءَانَسۡتُم مِّنۡهُمۡ رُشۡدٗا فَٱدۡفَعُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡۖ وَلَا تَأۡكُلُوهَآ إِسۡرَافٗا وَبِدَارًا أَن يَكۡبَرُواْۚ وَمَن كَانَ غَنِيّٗا فَلۡيَسۡتَعۡفِفۡۖ وَمَن كَانَ فَقِيرٗا فَلۡيَأۡكُلۡ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ فَإِذَا دَفَعۡتُمۡ إِلَيۡهِمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ فَأَشۡهِدُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ
phrases.translation: Test ˹the competence of˺ the orphans until they reach a marriageable age. Then if you feel they are capable of sound judgment, return their wealth to them. And do not consume it wastefully and hastily before they grow up ˹to demand it˺. If the guardian is well-off, they should not take compensation; but if the guardian is poor, let them take a reasonable provision. When you give orphans back their property,
phrases.explanation:
"Test the orphans until they reach a marriageable age. Then if you feel they are capable of sound judgment, hand over their wealth to them. Do not consume or squander it in haste, fearing they will grow up and claim it. Whoever is well-off should refrain from taking it, and whoever is poor should take only what is reasonable. When you hand over their wealth, call witnesses. And Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner."

Allah commands the guardians to test the orphans until they reach the age of marriage, and "the age of marriage" means sexual maturity, the onset of puberty, as the exegetes explained. "And if you perceive in them sound judgment": the reciters differed over the reading, but the meaning is that if the guardian perceives in them sound discretion, that is intellect, uprightness in religion, and competence in managing their property. The exegetes differed over "sound judgment": some said it is intellect and uprightness in religion, others uprightness in religion and competence in managing property.

"Hand over their wealth to them": when the orphan reaches maturity and shows sound judgment, the guardian must give him his wealth, for it is his right, and withholding it beyond that is wrong. "Do not consume or squander it in haste, fearing they will grow up and claim it": do not eat the orphan's wealth or spend it wastefully before he comes of age, out of fear that he will grow up and take it, for that is injustice. "Whoever is well-off should refrain": if the guardian is rich, let him not take any portion of the orphan's wealth as payment for his guardianship. "And whoever is poor should take only what is reasonable": if he is poor, let him take from it only what is customary and reasonable for his work in guarding the orphan. "When you hand over their wealth, call witnesses": bring witnesses at the handover so that there is no dispute or denial later, and the orphan's right is protected. "And Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner": Allah knows all transactions, reckons every deed, and will hold the guardian to account, so fear Him and be honest in the orphan's wealth. "Sound judgment" the exegetes took variously as intellect alone, uprightness and knowledge of what benefits him, or uprightness in religion and competence in property, but all agree it is not permissible to withhold the wealth from the orphan once he has reached maturity and shows sound intellect and competence, so the correct meaning is uprightness and competence together. "Do not consume them by extravagance": the original meaning of extravagance is exceeding the permitted limit, and the guardian must not spend the orphan's wealth beyond what is permitted. "Nor in haste lest they grow up": the haste is only of the managers of the orphan's property, who fear the orphan will grow up and claim it, so they consume it first and the grammar of "lest" shows the haste belongs to them. "Whoever is well-off should refrain": the rich guardian should not take from the orphan's wealth, and some said "refrain" means the loan he borrows from the orphan's property which he then repays. "Whoever is poor should take only what is reasonable": the poor guardian may eat from it in a fitting manner, and those who held this differed over what "fitting" means: some said he eats of his food, others that he eats what stills his hunger and wears what covers him, others that he eats the dates and drinks the milk of the livestock he oversees, and others that he may eat of the property if he manages it, but all agree the manager owns nothing of the orphan's property except what is reasonable for his care of it. So test them well before handing over, and do not be hasty, for the wealth is a trust and Allah will ask about it. The orphan has a right to his wealth, and the guardian is only a trustee, so when the orphan shows maturity and sound judgment, give him his wealth in full, with witnesses present, and fear Allah in every dinar of it, for the Reckoner sees all. And whoever fears Allah in the orphan's wealth will be safe on the Day of Judgment.

phrases.ar: وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبٗا
phrases.translation: call in witnesses. And sufficient is Allah as a ˹vigilant˺ Reckoner
phrases.explanation: "When you hand over their wealth, call witnesses. And Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner." At the handover of the orphan's wealth, witnesses should be present to testify to it, so that the wealth is protected and no one can later deny the transaction. And Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner: He knows all that is done, reckons every deed, and will judge between the guardian and the orphan with justice, so be honest and fear Him. And the guardian will be asked about the wealth on the Day of Judgment. And witnesses are a protection for the orphan. And do not delay the handover once he is mature.

phrases.ar: لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٞ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَانِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبُونَ وَلِلنِّسَآءِ نَصِيبٞ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَانِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبُونَ مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنۡهُ أَوۡ كَثُرَۚ نَصِيبٗا مَّفۡرُوضٗا
phrases.translation: For men there is a share in what their parents and close relatives leave, and for women there is a share in what their parents and close relatives leave—whether it is little or much. ˹These are˺ obligatory shares
phrases.explanation: "For men there is a share in what their parents and close relatives leave, and for women there is a share in what their parents and close relatives leave, whether small or large, a fixed share." Allah establishes inheritance for both men and women: each has a prescribed share in what parents and close relatives leave, whether the amount is small or large. This was revealed because in the pre-Islamic era only the men inherited and the women were excluded, and some disinherited the weak. So Allah made the share of the female like a fixed portion, and the exegetes said the verse is general for all who inherit, male and female, and that the share is obligatory, not optional, for whoever is entitled to it.

phrases.ar: وَإِذَا حَضَرَ ٱلۡقِسۡمَةَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينُ فَٱرۡزُقُوهُم مِّنۡهُ وَقُولُواْ لَهُمۡ قَوۡلٗا مَّعۡرُوفٗا
phrases.translation: If ˹non-inheriting˺ relatives, orphans, or the needy are present at the time of distribution, offer them a ˹small˺ provision from it and speak to them kindly
phrases.explanation: "If non-inheriting relatives, orphans, or the needy are present at the time of distribution, offer them a small provision from it, and speak to them kindly." Allah commands that when the estate is divided, if relatives who do not inherit, orphans, or the poor are present, a small provision should be given to them from the estate before division, and kind words spoken to them. The exegetes differed over whether this is obligatory or recommended, some saying it is in force and others that it is a recommendation, but all agree it is better to give something to those present and to speak kindly, for that is generosity and good conduct, and Allah loves the doers of good. When the heirs gather to divide the estate, and near relatives who do not inherit, orphans, and the needy are present, give them a portion of the wealth as a gift before the division, and speak to them with kind and gentle words, saying that this is from the bounty of Allah. The exegetes differed over whether the provision is obligatory or recommended, some saying the verse is in force and others that it is a recommendation, but both sides agree that giving a little to those present and speaking kindly is better than arguing with them, and Allah is All-Seeing of what you do, so be generous at the time of division and do not send them away empty-handed or with harsh words, for the dead has no need of the wealth while the living do.

phrases.ar: وَلۡيَخۡشَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَوۡ تَرَكُواْ مِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّةٗ ضِعَٰفًا خَافُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ فَلۡيَتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلۡيَقُولُواْ قَوۡلٗا سَدِيدًا
phrases.translation: Let the guardians be as concerned ˹for the orphans˺ as they would if they were to ˹die and˺ leave ˹their own˺ helpless children behind. So let them be mindful of Allah and speak equitably
phrases.explanation: "Let the guardians be as concerned for the orphans as they would if they were to die and leave their own helpless children behind, so let them fear Allah and speak in a right and proper manner." The guardian should treat the orphan as he would want his own children to be treated if he died and left them weak and helpless behind him. The exegetes differed: some said the verse addresses those present with the testator at the making of his will, telling them to fear Allah and speak rightly to the orphans, and others that it is addressed to the guardians in general. Either way, the meaning is: fear Allah in the orphan's affair, speak to him in a right manner, give him his right, and do not devour his wealth, for Allah sees what you do. It is said this verse was revealed concerning a man who had daughters and a will, and the guardians are told to fear Allah in the orphan's wealth and to speak to him in a right manner, with sound speech that gives him hope and reminds him of Allah. And do not leave him a poor inheritance or wrong him in it, for you would want the same for your own children if you died and left weak offspring behind you. So fear Allah and say what is right, for Allah hears what you say and sees what you do.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡكُلُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَ ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ ظُلۡمًا إِنَّمَا يَأۡكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمۡ نَارٗاۖ
phrases.translation: Indeed, those who unjustly consume orphans’ wealth ˹in fact˺ consume nothing but fire into their bellies.
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those who unjustly consume orphans' wealth in fact consume nothing but fire into their bellies. And they will burn in a blazing Fire." Allah says: whoever eats the orphan's wealth unjustly only fills his belly with fire. "They will burn" is derived from warming oneself at a fire, and "a blazing Fire" is the Fire of Hell, which blazes and flames. So the unjust consumer of the orphan's wealth will enter the blazing Fire on the Day of Judgment and abide in it, and his crime is among the greatest of sins, for the orphan's wealth is a trust and Allah has made it a cause of entering the Fire.

phrases.ar: وَسَيَصۡلَوۡنَ سَعِيرٗا
phrases.translation: And they will be burned in a blazing Hell
phrases.explanation: "And they will burn in a blazing Fire." The blazing Fire is prepared for them, and it will enclose them, and they will not come out of it. The Fire is blazing and prepared, and it will seize them on the Day of Judgment, and they will abide in it forever, and nothing of the wealth they consumed will avail them then, for it was fire that they ate and fire that they will be burned with. So fear Allah, O guardians, and return the wealth. And the Fire will not be lightened for them. And their punishment is severe. And none of their good deeds will avail them.

phrases.ar: يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيٓ أَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡۖ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثۡلُ حَظِّ ٱلۡأُنثَيَيۡنِۚ فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءٗ فَوۡقَ ٱثۡنَتَيۡنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَۖ وَإِن كَانَتۡ وَٰحِدَةٗ فَلَهَا ٱلنِّصۡفُۚ وَلِأَبَوَيۡهِ لِكُلِّ وَٰحِدٖ مِّنۡهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِن كَانَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٞۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلَدٞ وَوَرِثَهُۥٓ أَبَوَاهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلثُّلُثُۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُۥٓ إِخۡوَةٞ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلسُّدُسُۚ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةٖ يُوصِي بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٍۗ ءَابَآؤُكُمۡ وَأَبۡنَآؤُكُمۡ لَا تَدۡرُونَ أَيُّهُمۡ أَقۡرَبُ لَكُمۡ نَفۡعٗاۚ
phrases.translation: Allah commands you regarding your children: the share of the male will be twice that of the female. If you leave only two ˹or more˺ females, their share is two-thirds of the estate. But if there is only one female, her share will be one-half. Each parent is entitled to one-sixth if you leave offspring. But if you are childless and your parents are the only heirs, then your mother will receive one-third. But if you leave siblings, then your mother will receive one-sixth—after the fulfilment of bequests and debts. ˹Be fair to˺ your parents and children, as you do not
phrases.explanation: "Allah commands you regarding your children: the share of the male will be twice that of the female. If you leave only two or more girls, their share is two-thirds of the estate. If there is only one, her share is half. Parents inherit one-sixth each if you have a child. If you have no children but your parents inherit, then one-sixth is for your mother. If you have brothers, your mother gets one-sixth. And these are after the will you have made and the debts you owe. Your parents and your children, you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit. Allah has ordained this, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Allah legislates the shares of inheritance for children: the male gets twice the share of the female, because the man bears the duty of spending on the family and fighting in the cause of Allah. If the children are only daughters, two or more, they get two-thirds of the estate, and if only one daughter, she gets half. The parents each get one-sixth if the deceased left a child, and if there are no children but parents inherit, the mother gets one-sixth, and if the deceased has brothers, the mother's share is one-sixth after the will and debts. The grammar shows "mithl" stands in the nominative as an attribute. "These are after the will and debts": the shares are distributed after paying the bequest up to one-third and the debts, for the debt comes before the inheritance. "You do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit": neither the parents nor the children can be known to be more beneficial, so Allah has ordained the shares for both. And this is a legislation from Allah, All-Knowing of what is best for His servants, All-Wise in His ruling. If the children left are only women, more than two, then for them is two-thirds of what he left, and the grammarians differed whether "women" here means the daughters or the children who are women, but the meaning is the daughters. If there is only one daughter, her share is half, and the share of exactly two daughters was established by the transmitted Sunna as two-thirds. For the parents, each gets one-sixth if the deceased left a child, and if he left no child and the parents inherit, the mother gets one-third and the father the rest, for he is the nearest relative. And if the deceased has brothers, the mother gets one-sixth. The exegetes differed over how many brothers reduce the mother to one-sixth: the majority of the companions and successors said two or more, since the minimum plural is two, while others narrated that even one brother reduces it. The grammar of the verse shows the shares are detailed with precision, and the reason the father is not named in the mother's share is that he takes the remainder as the nearest relative. And all of this is after the will up to one-third and after the debts, for the debt is paid before the inheritance and the bequest is honored within its limit. The exegetes differed over why the mother is reduced to one-sixth when there are brothers: some said the mother was diminished by the sixth as assistance to the brothers, because the father bears their maintenance, and others narrated the opposite. "After a bequest or a debt": the community agrees the shares are distributed after the bequest, which may not exceed one-third without the heirs' consent, and after the debt, which takes precedence over inheritance. The reciters differed over the passive reading of "bequeathed". And "you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit": the exegetes differed, some saying you do not know whether the parent or the child will be more beneficial to you in this life by his prayers or in the next by his intercession, so Allah gave a share to both. This legislation is from Allah, and surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise, and He knows what is best for His servants and has made the shares clear so that there is no dispute. The reason the male takes twice the female is that the man is responsible for spending on the woman and the family, while the woman is provided for, so the shares are equitable in light of the duties. And the will is honored first, but only up to one-third of the estate, and only for one who is not an heir, for the heir gets nothing from the will, and the debt is settled before everything, for the right of the creditor precedes the right of the heir. And whoever divides the estate according to this Book is upon clear guidance, and whoever alters it wrongs himself, and Allah sees it. And this is the justice of Allah in inheritance, clear and detailed, so that no heir is wronged and no dispute arises, and Allah has spoken the truth in His Book.

phrases.ar: فَرِيضَةٗ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمٗا
phrases.translation: ˹fully˺ know who is more beneficial to you. ˹This is˺ an obligation from Allah. Surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: "Your parents and your children, you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit. Allah has ordained this, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Allah has made inheritance for both parents and children, and you cannot know which is nearer to you in benefit in this life or the next, so He has ordained it, and surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise, and He knows what is best for you, so accept His legislation and do not prefer one over another unjustly. And obey this legislation, for it is from the All-Knowing, All-Wise. And He will reward the just and punish the unjust. And He is the best of legislators.

phrases.ar: ۞ وَلَكُمۡ نِصۡفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزۡوَٰجُكُمۡ إِن لَّمۡ يَكُن لَّهُنَّ وَلَدٞۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٞ فَلَكُمُ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكۡنَۚ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةٖ يُوصِينَ بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٖۚ وَلَهُنَّ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكۡتُمۡ إِن لَّمۡ يَكُن لَّكُمۡ وَلَدٞۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَكُمۡ وَلَدٞ فَلَهُنَّ ٱلثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكۡتُمۚ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةٖ تُوصُونَ بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٖۗ وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٞ يُورَثُ كَلَٰلَةً أَوِ ٱمۡرَأَةٞ وَلَهُۥٓ أَخٌ أَوۡ أُخۡتٞ فَلِكُلِّ وَٰحِدٖ مِّنۡهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُۚ فَإِن كَانُوٓاْ أَكۡثَرَ مِن ذَٰلِكَ فَهُمۡ شُرَكَآءُ فِي ٱلثُّلُثِۚ
phrases.translation: You will inherit half of what your wives leave if they are childless. But if they have children, then ˹your share is˺ one-fourth of the estate—after the fulfilment of bequests and debts. And your wives will inherit one-fourth of what you leave if you are childless. But if you have children, then your wives will receive one-eighth of your estate—after the fulfilment of bequests and debts. And if a man or a woman leaves neither parents nor children but only a brother or a sister ˹from their mother’s side˺, they will each inherit one-sixth, but if they are more than one, they ˹all˺ will share one-third of the estate—after the fulfilment
phrases.explanation: "You will inherit half of what your wives leave if they are childless. But if they have children, then your share is a quarter. These shares are after any will they may have made or debt they owe. They will inherit a quarter of what you leave if you are childless, and an eighth if you have a child. If a man or woman is inherited by distant relatives and has a brother or sister, each gets one-sixth. But if there are more than one, they share the one-third. These shares are after any will or debt. And Allah does not let anyone go astray, for He is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing." Allah details the shares between spouses and others: the husband gets half of what the wife leaves if she has no child, and a quarter if she has a child. The wife gets a quarter of what the husband leaves if he has no child, and an eighth if he has a child. These are after the will and the debt, for debts and bequests come first. And if a man or a woman dies leaving no spouse or child, but is inherited by distant relatives, the kalala, and has a brother or a sister, each of them gets one-sixth, and if there are several brothers and sisters, they share one-third together. And Allah has legislated all this, and He is All-Knowing of what is best, Most Forbearing, and He does not wrong anyone in the shares. "A man inherited as kalala": the reciters differed over the reading, and the exegetes differed over the meaning of kalala, some saying it is the one who has no parent and no child, others that it is what is apart from the child, others that it excludes the father. And if the kalala has a brother or a sister, each gets one-sixth, but if there are more than one brother and sister, they share one-third together, male and female alike in this case. And the bequest is mentioned before the debt in the verse for emphasis, but both come before the shares. And Allah has made all this clear, and He is All-Knowing of who deserves what, Most Forbearing toward His servants, and He does not wrong anyone in an atom's weight. The grammarians differed over the case of "kalala": some made it the predicate of "was", saying the deceased is the kalala when he has no parent or child, others that the kalala are the heirs themselves, brothers, sisters, or others who inherit from him. And the share of the brother or sister of the kalala is one-sixth each, and if they are more than one they share the one-third, and in this case male and female are equal, unlike the case of children where the male takes twice the female. And Allah has legislated all of this with wisdom, and He is All-Knowing of the heirs and Most Forbearing, so obey His shares and do not alter them. And the shares are a mercy from Allah to the heirs. And He is All-Knowing.

phrases.ar: مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةٖ يُوصَىٰ بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٍ غَيۡرَ مُضَآرّٖۚ وَصِيَّةٗ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٞ
phrases.translation: of bequests and debts without harm ˹to the heirs˺. ˹This is˺ a commandment from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing
phrases.explanation: "And Allah does not let anyone go astray. He is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing." Allah knows the shares and the deserving heirs, and He is Most Forbearing, so He does not hasten the punishment of the one who errs in the division, but He will hold everyone to account, and He does not let the truth go astray, for He has made the shares clear in His Book. So fear Allah in the division of the estates. And whoever divides justly has succeeded. And He does not wrong anyone. And most kind to His servants, so fear Him in the division. And He knows what is in the hearts.

phrases.ar: تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ يُدۡخِلۡهُ جَنَّٰتٖ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ وَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
phrases.translation: These ˹entitlements˺ are the limits set by Allah. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever. That is the ultimate triumph
phrases.explanation: "These entitlements are the limits set by Allah. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted by Him into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and that is the supreme triumph." Allah has legislated the shares of inheritance and other entitlements, and these are His limits: obey them and do not exceed them. The exegetes differed over the meaning of "limits", some saying they are the obligatory duties and prohibitions, others the specific shares of inheritance, but all agree they are the boundary between the lawful and the unlawful. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and keeps within His limits will enter Paradise, gardens with flowing rivers, to abide forever, and that is the great success, for no success is greater than entering Paradise and being saved from the Fire. The limits of Allah are also His prohibitions: do not approach them, for whoever approaches them has transgressed, and whoever keeps away from them is safe. So obey Allah and His Messenger, keep to the shares He ordained, avoid what He forbade, and you will attain the supreme triumph, which is Paradise forever.

phrases.ar: وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُۥ يُدۡخِلۡهُ نَارًا خَٰلِدٗا فِيهَا وَلَهُۥ عَذَابٞ مُّهِينٞ
phrases.translation: But whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and exceeds their limits will be cast into Hell, to stay there forever. And they will suffer a humiliating punishment
phrases.explanation: "But whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and exceeds their limits will be cast into Hell, abiding therein forever, and they will have a humiliating punishment." Allah warns those who disobey Him and His Messenger and transgress His limits: they will be cast into Hell and abide in it forever, and they will have a humiliating, painful punishment. The verse pairs obedience with Paradise and disobedience with Hell, so that the believer hastens to obedience and avoids disobedience, for the punishment is everlasting and humiliating, and there is no escape from it except through the mercy of Allah. And the punishment is humiliating because it is everlasting.

phrases.ar: وَٱلَّٰتِي يَأۡتِينَ ٱلۡفَٰحِشَةَ مِن نِّسَآئِكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَشۡهِدُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ أَرۡبَعَةٗ مِّنكُمۡۖ فَإِن شَهِدُواْ فَأَمۡسِكُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلۡبُيُوتِ حَتَّىٰ يَتَوَفَّىٰهُنَّ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ أَوۡ يَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلٗا
phrases.translation: ˹As for˺ those of your women who commit illegal intercourse—call four witnesses from among yourselves. If they testify, confine the offenders to their homes until they die or Allah ordains a ˹different˺ way for them
phrases.explanation: "As for those of your women who commit illegal intercourse, call four witnesses from among you. If they testify, confine the women to houses until death takes them or Allah ordains a way for them. And those of your men who commit it, discipline them. If they repent and mend their ways, leave them alone. Allah is All-Accepting of repentance, Most Merciful." Allah legislates the punishment for the woman who commits the abomination: call four just witnesses from among the Muslims against her, and if they testify to it, confine her in her house until she dies or until Allah opens a way for her, which He did by legislating stoning in another verse. And the two men who commit the sin, hurt and discipline them with words and action, but if they repent and reform, leave them alone, for Allah accepts repentance and is Most Merciful to His servants who return to Him.

phrases.ar: وَٱلَّذَانِ يَأۡتِيَٰنِهَا مِنكُمۡ
phrases.translation: And the two among you who commit this sin—discipline
phrases.explanation: "And the two among you who commit this sin, discipline them both." Allah commands disciplining the two among you, man and woman, who commit this sin. The exegetes differed over who is meant by "the two": some said a man and a woman, others two men, others a slave and a slave woman, and they differed over the manner of the hurt, whether it is the prescribed punishment or a rebuke. In any case, the verse enjoins disciplining the sinners, then leaving them if they repent. Others said a man and a woman, except that no unmarried person apart from a previously married one is meant. And they differed over the hurt meant, whether the prescribed limit or a rebuke, but the preferred view is that the verse came down concerning the two unmarried sinners before the prescribed punishments were revealed, and then the limits were legislated.

phrases.ar: فَـَٔاذُوهُمَاۖ فَإِن تَابَا وَأَصۡلَحَا فَأَعۡرِضُواْ عَنۡهُمَآۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ تَوَّابٗا رَّحِيمًا
phrases.translation: them. If they repent and mend their ways, relieve them. Surely Allah is ever Accepting of Repentance, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: "If they repent and mend their ways, leave them alone. Allah is All-Accepting of repentance, Most Merciful." If the two of them repent and mend their ways, then leave them alone and do not pursue them, for Allah is All-Accepting of repentance, accepting it from whoever turns to Him, and Most Merciful, so He forgives the sin and covers it. So hasten to repentance before the punishment comes, and know that Allah accepts the repentance of His servants and is merciful to them. The exegetes agreed that leaving them alone after repentance is obligatory, for pursuing them after they have repented is wrong, and Allah loves those who forgive and turn away from the sinners who reform. And the mercy of Allah is vast, so whoever repents sincerely, Allah accepts, and whoever delays, let him know that death comes suddenly. Repentance means: turning to Allah, regretting the sin, resolving not to return to it, and restoring the rights of people. When the sinner does this, Allah accepts, and He is All-Accepting of repentance, Most Merciful, and He rejoices at the repentance of His servant more than one of you rejoices when he finds his lost mount.

phrases.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلتَّوۡبَةُ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ لِلَّذِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلسُّوٓءَ بِجَهَٰلَةٖ ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِن قَرِيبٖ
phrases.translation: Allah only accepts the repentance of those who commit evil ignorantly ˹or recklessly˺ then repent soon
phrases.explanation: "Allah only accepts the repentance of those who commit evil ignorantly or recklessly then repent soon after. It is they whose repentance Allah will accept. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Allah accepts repentance only from those who do evil out of ignorance or recklessness, then hasten to repent soon after, before death comes. The exegetes differed over the meaning: some said ignorance here means doing the sin without intending it, others that it is every sin done before the doer knows it is a sin, and others that it means the sin done in a moment of anger or passion. But all agree that the repentance accepted is the one that comes quickly, before the soul is taken, for Allah is All-Knowing of what is in the hearts and All-Wise in accepting the repentance of those who hasten to Him. Some said the ignorance means the sin itself is done in ignorance of its being a sin, others that the evil is done knowingly but the doer is ignorant of its punishment, and others that it is the sin done in a moment of anger, passion, or intoxication before the person is aware. But all of them agreed that the condition is that the repentance comes soon after, before the pangs of death, for when the soul reaches the throat, repentance is of no avail. And Allah is All-Knowing, knowing the sincerity of the repentant, and All-Wise in legislating that the hasty repentance is accepted and the delayed one is not. And whoever repents sincerely before death, Allah accepts from him, for the door of repentance is open until the sun rises from the west or the soul reaches the throat. And the wisdom in accepting the hasty repentance is to encourage the sinner to return to Allah quickly, while the wisdom in rejecting the delayed one is to prevent the sinner from trifling with sin and repenting only at the end.

phrases.ar: فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَتُوبُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمۡۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمٗا
phrases.translation: after—Allah will pardon them. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: "Allah only accepts the repentance of those who commit evil ignorantly then repent soon after." The hasty repentance is accepted, and the delay is not, until death comes. So do not delay your repentance, for you do not know when death will come, and the accepted repentance is the one that is hasty, sincere, with resolve not to return to the sin, and done before the soul is taken. And the condition of acceptance is sincerity and resolve, so repent now while the time remains. And Allah knows who is sincere, and He is All-Knowing, All-Wise. So turn to Him now, before it is too late. And do not despair.

phrases.ar: وَلَيۡسَتِ ٱلتَّوۡبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ إِنِّي تُبۡتُ ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ وَلَا ٱلَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمۡ كُفَّارٌۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابًا أَلِيمٗا
phrases.translation: However, repentance is not accepted from those who knowingly persist in sin until they start dying, and then cry, “Now I repent!” nor those who die as disbelievers. For them We have prepared a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: "However, repentance is not accepted from those who knowingly persist in sin until they start to see the punishment, then say, now I repent. Nor from those who die disbelievers. It is they who will have a painful punishment." Allah says that repentance is not accepted from those who keep doing evil knowingly until the punishment comes upon them and they see death approaching, and then they say, now I repent: their repentance is not accepted. Nor is it accepted from those who die while disbelieving. The scholars differed over who is meant: some said the hypocrites who persist in unbelief, others the sinners who delay until death. In both cases, they will have a painful punishment prepared for them in the Hereafter, and no repentance will avail them then, so repent before death and do not delay.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرۡهٗاۖ وَلَا تَعۡضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذۡهَبُواْ بِبَعۡضِ مَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٖ مُّبَيِّنَةٖۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ فَإِن كَرِهۡتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن
phrases.translation: O believers! It is not permissible for you to inherit women against their will or mistreat them to make them return some of the dowry ˹as a ransom for divorce˺—unless they are found guilty of adultery. Treat them fairly. If you happen to dislike them, you
phrases.explanation: "O believers! It is not permissible for you to inherit women against their will or to withhold from them what Allah has given them in order to take some of what you had given them, unless they remit some of it willingly. And be kind to one another. Allah is indeed All-Knowing of what you do." Allah forbids the believers from inheriting women against their will, which was the custom of the pre-Islamic Arabs, who would seize the wife of a dead relative along with his wealth, and forbids withholding from the wife part of what the husband gave her in order to pressure her into giving up her rights. If the husband wants to take back some of the dowry, that is not allowed unless the wife willingly gives it up, for the dowry is her right. And be kind to one another in your dealings, for Allah is All-Knowing of what you do, and He will requite every doer of good. The exegetes discussed how the inheritance happened before the prohibition and what its basis was, and agreed that the verse abrogates the old custom and establishes that the woman inherits only her prescribed share. The exegetes differed over the meaning of inheriting women against their will: some said it means taking the wife of the deceased along with his estate by force, which the heirs used to do, and others said it means taking the women's estates against their will while preventing them from remarrying, so that the heir keeps their wealth. Either way, Allah has forbidden it and made clear that the woman inherits only her share, and that what the husband holds of her is only through a valid marriage contract. "Nor to put them under pressure in order to take back a part of what you have given them": some said it means do not hold them by force and harm them to make them give up their rights, others that it means do not wrong them in the dowry. So be kind to one another, treat the women with justice, give them their rights, and Allah is All-Knowing of what you do, and He will judge between you on the Day of Judgment. Others said the women put under pressure are the wives, that you should not hold them in a harmful marriage to take back part of the dowry, and others said they are the guardians, who should not pressure the women to give up their inheritance. In all the views, the meaning is to forbid injustice toward women in their wealth, and to enjoin kindness between the spouses. And whoever wrongs a woman in her wealth, Allah will take him to account, for He is All-Knowing and All-Seeing, and He does not wrong anyone. And the believer should fear Allah in his dealings with women, for the weak are a trust, and He will ask about every right that is withheld.

phrases.ar: تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـٔٗا وَيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيۡرٗا كَثِيرٗا
phrases.translation: may hate something which Allah turns into a great blessing
phrases.explanation: "Unless they remit some of it willingly. And be kind to one another. Allah is indeed All-Knowing of what you do." If the wife forgives the husband part of her right willingly and of her own accord, that is permissible, and it is a good deed that Allah will reward. And be kind to one another, and Allah is All-Knowing of your dealings. And kindness in this matter is to treat her well, not to pressure her, and to accept what she forgives willingly. And Allah is All-Knowing, seeing the intention of the doer, and He will reward the kind and punish the unjust. And He sees it.

phrases.ar: وَإِنۡ أَرَدتُّمُ ٱسۡتِبۡدَالَ زَوۡجٖ مَّكَانَ زَوۡجٖ وَءَاتَيۡتُمۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُنَّ قِنطَارٗا فَلَا تَأۡخُذُواْ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـًٔاۚ
phrases.translation: If you desire to replace a wife with another and you have given the former ˹even˺ a stack of gold ˹as a dowry˺, do not take any of it
phrases.explanation: "If you desire to replace a wife with another and you have given the former a great amount of wealth, do not take any of it back. Would you take it back while having done so to her an obvious wrong?" Allah permits replacing one wife with another by divorcing the first, but forbids taking back anything of the qintar, the great amount of wealth, that was given to her, for taking it back after intimacy and a shared life is an obvious wrong and an injustice. The exegetes mentioned the disagreement over the amount of the qintar, some saying it is a large amount of gold, others that it is whatever was given generously, but all agree that taking it back is forbidden, for the dowry belongs to the wife, and Allah has made taking it back a clear wrong.

phrases.ar: أَتَأۡخُذُونَهُۥ بُهۡتَٰنٗا وَإِثۡمٗا مُّبِينٗا
phrases.translation: back. Would you ˹still˺ take it unjustly and very sinfully
phrases.explanation: "Would you take it back while having done so to her an obvious wrong?" No, you would not, for it is a clear injustice, and Allah knows what you do. Taking back the wealth after intimacy and a shared life, when she has given herself to him and he has enjoyed her, is a clear wrong and an injustice, and Allah knows what you do, and He is All-Just, so do not take it back, and be kind to the divorced wife. And the wrong is obvious because the dowry was given to her as a gift and a right, and she has fulfilled the marriage, so taking it back is unjust.

phrases.ar: وَكَيۡفَ تَأۡخُذُونَهُۥ وَقَدۡ أَفۡضَىٰ بَعۡضُكُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضٖ
phrases.translation: And how could you take it back after having enjoyed each other intimately and she has
phrases.explanation: "And how could you take it back after having enjoyed each other intimately and she has taken from you a solemn covenant?" Allah reproaches the one who wants to take back the dowry after he and his wife have been intimate and she has given him herself, for the marriage contract was a solemn covenant between them, and the intimacy is a trust. The verse has the form of a question but its meaning is reproach and prohibition: how could you do that, when you have enjoyed each other and made a firm covenant, and she has entrusted herself to you. So take it back is not allowed, for that is a great sin.

phrases.ar: وَأَخَذۡنَ مِنكُم مِّيثَٰقًا غَلِيظٗا
phrases.translation: taken from you a firm commitment
phrases.explanation: "And she has taken from you a solemn covenant." The covenant is the marriage contract, and it is firm, so do not break it by taking back what you gave. "Going in to" means intimacy, and the exegetes explained it as the reaching of it, and said the statement, though a question, means reproach: how would you take what you gave her when you have been intimate with her and she has taken from you a solemn covenant, the firm marriage contract. And the exegetes agreed that the dowry is not returned to the husband after intimacy, unless the wife forgives it of her own accord, for the marriage contract is a great covenant and the wife has a right to the dowry, so taking it back is forbidden, and Allah is All-Knowing of what you do. The exegetes differed over the covenant: some said it is the marriage contract itself, others that it is holding the wife in a proper manner or releasing her with good treatment, and it was said of old in the marriage covenant that the husband would treat his wife well or release her kindly. So the covenant is firm, and breaking it by taking back the dowry is a great wrong, and Allah forbids it and knows what you do. And whoever fears Allah in this matter will be safe, for the covenant of marriage is before Allah and He is witness over all things. And do not be unjust. And He is witness.

phrases.ar: وَلَا تَنكِحُواْ مَا نَكَحَ ءَابَآؤُكُم مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلَّا مَا قَدۡ
phrases.translation: Do not marry former wives of your fathers—except what was done previously. It
phrases.explanation: "Do not marry former wives of your fathers, except what was done previously. It was indeed an indecent, shameful, and evil act." Allah forbids marrying the women whom your fathers married, even if they divorced them, except what was already done in the pre-Islamic era, which is forgiven. This was a custom among the Arabs, and Allah forbade it because it is indecent and shameful, and an evil opening that leads to corruption of lineage. So whoever did it before Islam is excused, but whoever does it after is sinning, for Allah has made it unlawful and the punishment for it is severe. The exegetes mentioned the narrations about this verse and its reason of revelation, and they differed over whether the exception covers all that was done before or only specific cases, but the ruling is clear: the prohibition is established after Islam, and the past is forgiven, for Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful to those who repent and desist. And Allah is All-Knowing.

phrases.ar: سَلَفَۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فَٰحِشَةٗ وَمَقۡتٗا وَسَآءَ سَبِيلًا
phrases.translation: was indeed a shameful, despicable, and evil practice
phrases.explanation: "It was indeed an indecent, shameful, and evil act." It is fahisha, indecency, and a detestable thing, and the doer of it is punished. And it was called fahisha because it is indecency that the sound nature rejects, and it is a detestable act that corrupts lineage and mixes lineages, so Allah forbade it and promised the doer a painful punishment. And whoever does it after Islam has no excuse, and his act is a major sin, for the lineages must be kept pure and clear. So avoid it and fear Allah. And repent to Allah if you have done it. And He is Most Merciful to those who turn back.

phrases.ar: حُرِّمَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أُمَّهَٰتُكُمۡ وَبَنَاتُكُمۡ وَأَخَوَٰتُكُمۡ وَعَمَّٰتُكُمۡ وَخَٰلَٰتُكُمۡ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلۡأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلۡأُخۡتِ وَأُمَّهَٰتُكُمُ ٱلَّٰتِيٓ أَرۡضَعۡنَكُمۡ وَأَخَوَٰتُكُم مِّنَ ٱلرَّضَٰعَةِ وَأُمَّهَٰتُ نِسَآئِكُمۡ وَرَبَٰٓئِبُكُمُ ٱلَّٰتِي فِي حُجُورِكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ ٱلَّٰتِي دَخَلۡتُم بِهِنَّ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَكُونُواْ دَخَلۡتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَحَلَٰٓئِلُ أَبۡنَآئِكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِنۡ أَصۡلَٰبِكُمۡ وَأَن تَجۡمَعُواْ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأُخۡتَيۡنِ إِلَّا مَا قَدۡ سَلَفَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورٗا رَّحِيمٗا
phrases.translation: ˹Also˺ forbidden to you for marriage are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal and maternal aunts, your brother’s daughters, your sister’s daughters, your foster-mothers, your foster-sisters, your mothers-in-law, your stepdaughters under your guardianship if you have consummated marriage with their mothers—but if you have not, then you can marry them—nor the wives of your own sons, nor two sisters together at the same time—except what was done previously. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: "Also forbidden to you for marriage are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, your nursing mothers, your nursing sisters, your mothers-in-law, and your stepdaughters under your guardianship born of your wives to whom you have gone in, but if you have not gone in to them there is no sin on you. And the wives of your sons who are from your loins, and that you not marry two sisters at once, except what was done previously. Allah is indeed All-Forgiving, Most Merciful." Allah lists the women forbidden in marriage: the mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal and maternal aunts, the nursing mothers and nursing sisters, the mothers-in-law, and the stepdaughters in one's guardianship, and the wives of one's own sons, and the combining of two sisters in marriage at the same time. The exceptions for what was done before are a forgiveness for the past. The stepdaughter is forbidden only if the husband went in to her mother, otherwise there is no sin. And Allah is All-Forgiving of what was done before Islam, Most Merciful to His servants, so whoever did it before is forgiven, and whoever does it after is sinning.

phrases.ar: ۞ وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۖ كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَأُحِلَّ لَكُم مَّا وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُم مُّحۡصِنِينَ
phrases.translation: Also ˹forbidden are˺ married women—except ˹female˺ captives in your possession. This is Allah’s commandment to you. Lawful to you are all beyond these—as long as you seek them with your wealth in a
phrases.explanation: "Also forbidden are married women, except female captives in your possession. This is Allah's decree upon you. Lawful to you are all beyond these, as long as you seek them with your wealth in a legal marriage, not in fornication. For those you have enjoyed, give them their due dowries. There is no blame on you for what is mutually agreed beyond the set terms. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Allah forbids married women, except the female captives that came into the possession of the Muslims, concerning which the verse was revealed, and the exegetes differed over the reason and over whether the exception covers only captives taken in a just war or others, but the ruling is that the captive woman's previous marriage is annulled. Beyond these forbidden categories, all women are lawful if sought with the dowry in a proper marriage, not fornication. And for the wives you have enjoyed, give them their due dowries, for the dowry is their right. And there is no blame for what husband and wife mutually agree beyond the set terms. And Allah is All-Knowing of what is best, All-Wise in His legislation.

phrases.ar: غَيۡرَ مُسَٰفِحِينَۚ فَمَا ٱسۡتَمۡتَعۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡهُنَّ فَـَٔاتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةٗۚ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِيمَا تَرَٰضَيۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡفَرِيضَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمٗا
phrases.translation: legal marriage, not in fornication. Give those you have consummated marriage with their due dowries. It is permissible to be mutually gracious regarding the set dowry. Surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: "This is Allah's decree upon you. Lawful to you are all beyond these. And there is no blame on you for what is mutually agreed beyond the set terms. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Allah has decreed the forbidden and the lawful, and made clear the limits, and beyond the forbidden all is lawful with a proper marriage. And after the set terms of the dowry, whatever the spouses mutually agree to give or forgive is permissible, for Allah has permitted that, and He is All-Knowing, All-Wise. The exegetes differed over al-muhsanat, the married or chaste women: some said they are the married women, others the chaste women, others the women of the People of the Book, others the free women, others the wives of the emigrants who were left behind, but all agreed that what is forbidden is marrying them except through a valid marriage with a dowry, while the captives in possession are excepted. And Allah has decreed this, and He is All-Knowing of what is best for His servants, All-Wise in His ruling. And the decree of Allah is firm, and no one can change it. And He is All-Wise. And He knows all.

phrases.ar: وَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ مِنكُمۡ طَوۡلًا أَن يَنكِحَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ فَمِن مَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُم مِّن فَتَيَٰتِكُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِۚ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِإِيمَٰنِكُمۚ بَعۡضُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡضٖۚ فَٱنكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذۡنِ أَهۡلِهِنَّ وَءَاتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ مُحۡصَنَٰتٍ غَيۡرَ مُسَٰفِحَٰتٖ وَلَا مُتَّخِذَٰتِ أَخۡدَانٖۚ فَإِذَآ أُحۡصِنَّ فَإِنۡ أَتَيۡنَ بِفَٰحِشَةٖ فَعَلَيۡهِنَّ نِصۡفُ مَا عَلَى ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنۡ خَشِيَ ٱلۡعَنَتَ مِنكُمۡۚ
phrases.translation: But if any of you cannot afford to marry a free believing woman, then ˹let him marry˺ a believing bondwoman possessed by one of you. Allah knows best ˹the state of˺ your faith ˹and theirs˺. You are from one another. So marry them with the permission of their owners, giving them their dowry in fairness, if they are chaste, neither promiscuous nor having secret affairs. If they commit indecency after marriage, they receive half the punishment of free women. This is for those of you who fear falling into sin.
phrases.explanation: "But if any of you cannot afford to marry a free believing woman, then marry a believing bondwoman in your possession. Allah knows best your faith, you are from one another. So marry them with the permission of their owners and give them their due dowries in a proper manner, chaste, not fornicating or taking secret lovers. If they commit indecency after marriage, they receive half the punishment of free women. This is for those of you who fear falling into sin. But to be patient is better for you. Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful." Allah permits the one who cannot afford the dowry of a free believing woman to marry a believing slave woman from those in his possession, with the permission of her owner, and to give her the dowry in a proper manner. Allah says He knows your faith better than you know it yourselves, and that you are all from one another, so the slave woman is not lower in religion before Allah. The reciters differed over the reading of the word describing them, some reading it as "chaste", others with a different vowel, meaning they made themselves chaste. And the exegetes discussed the young women, saying every slave girl, whether young or old, is included in the permission, and they differed over the dowry of the slave woman, whether it is less than that of the free woman. "Chaste, not fornicating or taking secret lovers": the slave woman must be chaste too, and if she commits indecency after marriage, her punishment is half that of the free woman, because she is under the authority of her master and her situation is weaker. "This is for those of you who fear falling into sin": the permission is for the one who fears fornication if he does not marry. But to be patient and not marry is better for you, for Allah is All-Forgiving of what was done before, Most Merciful to His servants, and He has made the religion easy and lightened the burdens. The scholars differed over the marrying of non-believing slave women: some said the verse indicates a prohibition, and others that it is guidance and exhortation, not prohibition, and they cited that the women of the People of the Book are lawful in marriage. And if someone asks how the verse in another chapter permits them through marriage, the answer is that that verse clarifies its ruling pertains to a specific portion of them, namely the chaste ones. "And Allah knows best concerning your faith, some of you more than others": He knows the reality of your faith, that some of you are more believing than others, and He knows who is deserving of the permission and who is not. And as for the word "part", it is in the nominative, and the meaning is: from those whom your right hands possess, and you are from one another, meaning you share the same religion and origin, so there is no disgrace in marrying the slave woman. And the exegetes said the verse was revealed concerning the companions who had slave women and wished to marry them, and Allah permitted it with the consent of the owners and a proper dowry. And the punishment of the slave woman for indecency is half, because of her weak situation under the authority of her master, and Allah is just, not wronging anyone. And the preference of patience over marrying is for the one who fears that he will not do justice, and Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful, and He has permitted this out of mercy and ease, and He knows what is best for you, and He guides whom He wills. And He commands marrying them with the permission of their owners and giving them their dowries according to what is customary, meaning what you have agreed upon, for the dowry is a right of the woman, whether free or slave. And they must be chaste, not fornicating and not taking secret lovers, for the slave woman is not permitted what is forbidden to the free woman. And if they commit indecency after marriage, then upon them is half the punishment that is upon free women, and the exegetes differed over the manner of the half, whether in the number of lashes or otherwise, but the preferred view is that the punishment is halved for the slave woman, and Allah is All-Knowing of what is right. And all of this is for those of you who fear harm, meaning falling into fornication, and marrying the slave woman protects him from sin. And to be patient is better, and Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful, and He forgives whoever restrains himself and does not marry, and He knows the weak and has mercy on them, and He has made the matter easy, and He guides whom He wills to the straight path, and He is All-Knowing, All-Wise. And whoever marries her must intend the marriage properly and treat her with kindness, for she is a believer like him, and Allah sees the intentions and the dealings, and He will reward the doer of good and punish the wrongdoer in this life and the next. And Allah is the best of helpers. And do not despair of the mercy of Allah, for He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

phrases.ar: وَأَن تَصۡبِرُواْ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ
phrases.translation: But if you are patient, it is better for you. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: "But to be patient is better for you. Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful." Patience and not marrying the slave woman is better for the one who can afford to wait for a free woman, for Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful, and He forgives the one who restrains himself, and He knows what is best for you. And the patient one will be rewarded, and Allah is All-Forgiving of the past, Most Merciful to His servants, and He does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. And patience is a noble quality. And whoever is patient, Allah is with the patient. And He knows all. And He is All-Knowing.

phrases.ar: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمۡ وَيَهۡدِيَكُمۡ سُنَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ وَيَتُوبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٞ
phrases.translation: It is Allah’s Will to make things clear to you, guide you to the ˹noble˺ ways of those before you, and turn to you in mercy. For Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: "It is Allah's Will to make things clear to you, guide you to the noble ways of those before you, and accept your repentance. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Allah says He wills to clarify for you His legislation, the lawful and the forbidden, and to guide you to the good conduct of the nations before you, who followed the guidance, and to accept your repentance and forgive your sins. And Allah is All-Knowing of what is best for His servants, All-Wise in what He legislates, and He has made the religion clear so that there is no confusion. And follow the guidance of those before you. And He is All-Wise.

phrases.ar: وَٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَيُرِيدُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ أَن تَمِيلُواْ مَيۡلًا عَظِيمٗا
phrases.translation: And it is Allah’s Will to turn to you in grace, but those who follow their desires wish to see you deviate entirely ˹from Allah’s Way˺
phrases.explanation: "And it is Allah's Will to turn to you in grace, but those who follow their desires want you to incline to a great deviation." Allah wills to show mercy to you and accept your repentance, but those who follow their desires, the people of sin and deviation, want you to incline with them to a great deviation from the truth. The scholars differed over who is meant by those who follow their desires: some said the Jews, others the fornicators, others the disbelievers, but the meaning is general for whoever follows his desires against the command of Allah, and Allah warns the believers against them, for following the desires leads to the Fire. And He wills your good.

phrases.ar: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمۡۚ وَخُلِقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ ضَعِيفٗا
phrases.translation: And it is Allah’s Will to lighten your burdens, for humankind was created weak
phrases.explanation: "And it is Allah's Will to lighten your burdens, for humankind was created weak." Allah wills to lighten your burdens and ease the legislation for you, for man was created weak, unable to bear hardship and inclined to follow his desires. So Allah legislated what is easy and lightened the burdens, out of His mercy to you, and He knows your weakness, so He does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. And He made the legislation easy and light, and He knows your weakness, so do not despair of His mercy. And do not burden yourselves beyond your strength. And He is Merciful. And He guides whom He wills.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَأۡكُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٰلَكُم بَيۡنَكُم بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً عَن تَرَاضٖ مِّنكُمۡۚ
phrases.translation: O believers! Do not devour one another’s wealth illegally, but rather trade by mutual consent. And do not kill ˹each
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Do not devour one another's wealth illegally, but rather trade by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves. Allah is indeed Merciful to you." Allah forbids the believers from consuming one another's wealth by falsehood, theft, usury, or unjust taking, and permits only trade by mutual consent, in which each party is pleased. And He forbids killing yourselves, meaning do not kill one another, and do not commit suicide. The exegetes differed over the reason: some said the verse prohibits a man eating the food of his brother except with his consent, others that it is a general prohibition of devouring wealth unjustly. In any case, the meaning is: take wealth only by a rightful transaction, and Allah is indeed Merciful to you, so He forbade the unjust and permitted the just. The falsehood by which Allah forbade consuming wealth includes theft, usury, bribery, gambling, cheating in trade, and every unjust taking, and the exception is commerce by mutual consent, a trade in which both parties agree willingly. The reciters differed over the reading of the exception, some with the nominative meaning unless there is commerce from mutual consent among you. And the view that the verse was about eating the food of one's brother falls outside the meaning of eating in falsehood and is not abrogating. So trade with consent, give each his right, and do not kill yourselves, and Allah is Merciful to you, so He permitted the lawful and forbade the unlawful. And fear Allah in your wealth. And whoever trades with consent has done good, and Allah will bless his wealth, and whoever devours unjustly, his wealth will not be blessed and he will be punished in the Hereafter.

phrases.ar: وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمۡ رَحِيمٗا
phrases.translation: other or˺ yourselves. Surely Allah is ever Merciful to you
phrases.explanation: "And do not kill yourselves. Allah is indeed Merciful to you." Do not kill yourselves and do not kill one another, for Allah is Merciful to you, and He has forbidden the taking of life unjustly, and He will punish the killer, for life is sacred and the believer is not to shed blood without right. And the killing of the soul is a great sin, and the killer will be punished, for Allah is Merciful but He is also severe in punishment, and He knows what you do. And He sees you. So fear Allah and do not kill. And He is severe in punishment. And He is All-Seeing.

phrases.ar: وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ عُدۡوَٰنٗا وَظُلۡمٗا فَسَوۡفَ نُصۡلِيهِ نَارٗاۚ وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرًا
phrases.translation: And whoever does this sinfully and unjustly, We will burn them in the Fire. That is easy for Allah
phrases.explanation: "And whoever does this sinfully and unjustly, We will burn them in the Fire. And that is easy for Allah." Allah warns whoever devours wealth unjustly and kills without right: He will cast them into the Fire, and that is easy for Allah, for He is All-Powerful over His servants. The exegetes differed over the meaning, some saying it also covers the one who kills himself, but the meaning is general for the unjust doer of these sins, and the Fire is his abode, and Allah does it with ease, and He is All-Able. And the Fire is prepared for the unjust, and that is easy for Allah, and He is All-Powerful.
